source.title: Repetitions are not all alike: distinct mechanisms sustain repetition in language models

record.tranche_reason: The study measures repetition and attention-head contributions across training checkpoints using a different method from the original induction-head and loss-curve analyses.
record.gate_note: The study tests ICL-induced repetition and its head activity over training, but does not identify the [A][B] … [A] → [B] induction-head circuit or measure its composition with a previous-token head. It does not report a training-loss bump or the usual loss-by-token-position measure of in-context learning. Its claims about natural repetition and attention to low-information tokens are not results on those specific induction-head claims. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tracks ICL-induced repetition (copying a sequence repeated in the prompt) and tuned-lens head contrast in Pythia 1.4B at 10 checkpoints. It never identifies induction heads: no prefix-matching or copying scores, no previous-token-head composition, no loss curve and no loss-by-token-index. Its head contrast is a related construct, not a measure of induction heads. The checkpoints are coarse: step 0, then 10k, 100k and the final step are named. Pythia's usual induction-head window lies between the first two, so abruptness of formation cannot be read. The findings are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as tests.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that ICL-induced repetition is a learned, progressively refined behaviour carried by specialized attention heads plus late-layer MLPs. Natural repetition appears early, lacks an identifiable circuit, and acts as an uncertainty-driven fallback that attends to low-information tokens. Both mechanisms persist and interact in the trained model.
record.recipe_differences: The study probes attention-head output contributions to cycle continuation and tracks repetition across checkpoints. It does not use the original induction-head identification/composition analysis or measure the original loss-curve and loss-by-token-position signals.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt condition changes the observed trajectory: natural repetition is early-available, whereas ICL-induced repetition increases gradually. The study also reports head contrast changing with cycle number.

fits_no_version.finding: In Pythia 1.4B, ICL-induced repetition of a repeated prompt is absent at step 0. It is minimal until step 10k, then rises gradually across the later checkpoints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavioural copying of repeated sequences grows gradually over training in Pythia 1.4B (coarse checkpoint resolution).

fits_no_version.finding: In the latest checkpoint, a few heads (layer 7, heads 2-8) carry polarized contrast favouring or opposing cycle continuation, strengthening with cycle number. At 10k/100k, heads flip contrast only from cycle 3 onward.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small set of specialized heads supports in-context copying-driven repetition and becomes pattern-agnostic late in training.

fits_no_version.finding: Natural repetition shows no head contrast beyond noise and appears from the first checkpoint.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Natural degenerate repetition does not rely on copying-head circuitry.

record.problems: The study focuses on one model, Pythia 1.4B. The relevant behavioral and head-development figures are not accompanied by numeric checkpoint values in the text. It does not measure the loss curve, general ICL loss-by-token-position, or causal composition with a previous-token head.

untested.parts: No induction attention pattern and no previous-token-head composition.
No induction-head detection, no loss bump, no in-context loss by token index. Checkpoints are too coarse to see an early abrupt window.
One model; heads are not identified as induction heads.
Data and training setup are not varied.
Formation sub-steps of induction heads are not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests' relation and its V2 challenges / V7 supports labels are removed. The study never identifies induction heads, and 10 checkpoints with 0 and 10k adjacent cannot speak to abrupt early formation. MLP contrast is first nonzero at step 10k (Appendix A). Entropy results are off-claim.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the induction pattern [A][B] … [A] → [B], attention to the token after an earlier copy, or composition with a previous-token head.
Does not measure a loss-curve bump or a sharp gain in in-context learning as loss falls with token index; its repetition and head-activity measures are not the original loss-curve measures.
Does not measure most in-context learning in large transformers or compare induction heads with other carriers of general ICL.
Uses Pythia 1.4B only; does not test universality across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
Does not vary training data or training setup to test their effect on induction-head formation or persistence of general ICL.
Does not study few-shot task learning or compare its mechanisms with induction heads.
Does not test whether the specific formation of induction heads consists of multiple separate sub-steps; it tracks ICL-induced repetition and head contrast over checkpoints.

rows.subject: Pythia 1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the proportion of ICL-prompt outputs exhibiting repetition across checkpoints.

conditions.value: ICL prompts made by repeating raw sequences that did not trigger repetition
10 checkpoints; exact checkpoint list not stated

rows.value: No repetitions at the first timestep; the proportion increased gradually, with prompts moving in and out of the repeating category.
rows.note: The authors describe a gradual behavioral increase, not an abrupt onset. The figure plots proportions, but no numeric values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Behavioural repetition proportion over 10 coarse checkpoints, not induction-head formation. Marking it 'reversed' against V2 is unwarranted: the measure cannot resolve an early narrow window, and no loss curve is reported.

rows.subject: Pythia 1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Measured attention-head contrast for continuing versus interrupting the cycle.
rows.measure: Attention-head contrast for the cycle token versus the most likely non-cycle token
rows.value: Contrast values were random from cycle to cycle and centered around 0.
rows.note: The authors say the model had not yet learned ICL-based repetition in this phase.
rows.check: Tuned-lens head contrast for cycle versus non-cycle tokens is not an induction-head measure. It does not bear on V2 or V7.

rows.subject: Pythia 1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Measured attention-head contrast for continuing versus interrupting the cycle.
rows.measure: Attention-head contrast for the cycle token versus the most likely non-cycle token
rows.value: Most heads had values between -.5e-6 and .5e-6; on cycle 3, a majority of heads changed contrast rapidly, with positive values dropping below zero and negative values moving the other way.
rows.note: The rapid change described is across cycles after a pattern becomes detectable, not a reported abrupt transition across training.
rows.check: The rapid change described happens across generation cycles within a prompt, not across training. It does not show sub-steps of induction-head formation.

rows.subject: Pythia 1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Measured attention-head contrast for continuing versus interrupting the cycle.

conditions.value: heads 2 to 8 from layer 7 identified as strongly activated

rows.measure: Attention-head contrast for the cycle token versus the most likely non-cycle token
rows.value: Heads 2 to 8 from layer 7 had increasingly polarized contrast values as cycle number increased; other heads remained at very low activations.
rows.locator: Section 3.3, ICL at latest training step; Figure 2
rows.note: This reports specialized heads contributing to ICL-induced repetition, but does not establish induction-head composition or the claimed loss-curve timing.
rows.check: Layer 7 heads 2-8 promote cycle continuation, but they are not shown to be induction heads (no attention-pattern or composition analysis).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that repetition increases gradually and head specialization develops over training, rather than appearing abruptly; the study does not test the claimed loss bump or aligned general-ICL gain. Rows R1-R4.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The results describe progressive behavioral development and an intermediate head-contrast pattern before the latest specialized-head state, consistent with development over multiple stages rather than a single abrupt transition. Rows R1-R4.
